Your records live in Cin7: Cin7 holds your customers, stock levels, invoices and lot numbers. We hold the guide you build for each account, with your prices, and the orders restaurants send through the app.

Portal and EDI accounts stay put: Customers using your Cin7 portal, and chains that send EDI, carry on as they are. Our app is aimed at restaurants still on the phone. A call that still comes to your office gets no number from us; only orders sent in the app do.
Keep Cin7's document reader for PO files: On Cin7 Core, an add-on called IDR reads a customer's PO file and turns it into a sale your team approves, so keep it for the accounts that send one.

@graph.name: Do we need a Cin7 alternative to take spoken orders from restaurants?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Your stock, and any webstore, portal or EDI you run, stay with Cin7. We add one more way in, for the restaurants that call you: a chef talks through the order in our app and goes over each item before it is sent.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Cin7?

acceptedAnswer.text: Better at one thing only: serving the restaurants that phone you. Their chefs get an app of their own to order in: speak, check, send. Cin7 runs inventory, batch records, buying from suppliers and your webstore and marketplace sales, and we run none of those, so we are not a Cin7 alternative.

@graph.name: We run Cin7 Omni, not Core. Does that change setup?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. On either edition, setup needs no Cin7 login and installs nothing: we work from a spreadsheet exported from Cin7, and your add-ons, automations and connections stay as they are. Omni has EDI built in for retail chains, while Core connects EDI through partners, so whether our orders could arrive the same way depends on your edition and setup. If you would like orders to arrive that way, the demo covers what it would take on your side.

@graph.name: Doesn't Cin7's B2B portal already let restaurants reorder?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can. The portal is an add-on where customers you invite log in, browse the catalog you set up, see past orders and reorder, and it works in a phone browser. Cin7 pitches it as a way to keep your customers' shelves stocked. Restaurants that use it should keep it. The app is for the chefs who still prefer to call.

@graph.name: Will someone at our desk still key these orders into Cin7?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the format. The products are separate, and each vendor supports its own software only. If Cin7 is configured to accept our orders as EDI or from the API, they need no retyping at all; we look at that with you in the demo. By email, someone still enters the sale, but from a file that was checked in the kitchen first, not from a call or a voicemail. Other tools are used beside Cin7 as well, such as readers for emailed purchase orders and AI agents that answer your phone. Ours is in the chef's hands.

@graph.name: Will app orders count in Cin7 reports like our other sales?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, once the order is in Cin7. Whether your desk enters it or it comes in as an EDI or API order where Cin7 is set up for it, it becomes a sale in Cin7 like any other and counts in your sales and stock figures. Before that, the order already carries our order number and a timestamp.

@graph.name: What will it cost us, and how soon can kitchens order?

acceptedAnswer.text: We get most distributors running in 24 to 48 hours. Cin7 publishes prices for its Core plans and quotes Omni; we quote every distributor separately and publish no prices. A Cin7 replacement would mean moving your stock, batches and every sales connection at once. Adding the app leaves all of that where it is.
